clue.text: Plant imitation jewel

parts.note: sham means fake or imitation
rock is slang for a gem, especially a diamond

explanation.surface: A houseplant sold alongside costume jewellery, or a fake gem described as a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-leafed clover emblem of Ireland is a small plant.

clue.text: Bribe reserve with gold nuggets, initially

parts.note: a sub is a substitute or reserve player
or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: initially says take the opening letter of the word nuggets

explanation.surface: Someone pays off a substitute with lumps of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: To induce someone to commit perjury or wrongdoing, typically by payment, is to bribe them.

clue.text: One representing another sister ringing old employer, perhaps

parts.note: an agent acts on behalf of someone else

indicators.note: ringing means surrounding, so one piece encircles the other

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister

explanation.surface: A rep has a sister phoning a former boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' looks like telephoning but means encircling. Grammatically 'employer' is a word for the one who employs, formed from a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Words like employer, built from a verb to name the doer, are an example of this grammatical category.

clue.text: All are crazy about English beer

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumble surrounds the other piece
crazy suggests the words go wild and their letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Everyone is mad about English ale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' turns ALL ARE into RALALE, and 'about' puts it round E. REAL ALE is British cask-conditioned beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional cask-conditioned ale is a type of beer.

clue.text: Greek character's dropped off French wine for trainee

indicators.note: dropped off says one piece is removed from the other

parts.note: Muscadet is a dry white wine from the Loire
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet, and the apostrophe-s is kept as a letter S

explanation.surface: A Greek has nodded off over a glass of French wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped off' reads as fell asleep but means removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A young person training for the armed forces or police is a trainee.

clue.text: Some brief is called in relating to financial matters

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lawyer is summoned to deal with money questions.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition began with 'in', which cannot stand for the answer; 'in' is a link word and the definition is 'relating to financial matters'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiscal is the adjective for public revenue, taxation and money affairs.

clue.text: Hymn trendy trio jazzed up after time

indicators.note: after places the jumbled letters behind the time letter

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: jazzed up suggests the word is livened and rearranged

explanation.surface: A fashionable trio makes a jazz arrangement of a hymn after a delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trendy trio' looks like one phrase, but 'trendy' gives IN on its own; 'jazzed up' shuffles the trio and 'after' sets it behind T.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm or antiphon sung at the opening of a church service is a hymn.

clue.text: Instrument in hermit's place, nothing in addition

indicators.note: in addition says the second piece is added on

parts.note: a cell is a hermit's small dwelling
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: There is a musical instrument in a hermit's home, and nothing else.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bowed stringed instrument is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Audience member somehow riles number inside

indicators.note: inside says the number goes within the jumbled letters
somehow suggests the letters are made into something by some other arrangement

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: Someone in the crowd is irritated by a number on the programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' scrambles the verb 'riles', and 'inside' sends a number into the middle of the scramble; 'number' here is ten, not a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A person hearing a radio show or talk is one of its audience.

clue.text: Exclude workers in tightly-fitting trousers

parts.note: to skip is to omit or exclude
worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: A dress code bans staff wearing tight trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretchy close-fitting leggings worn on the slopes are a kind of trousers.

clue.text: Street band likes playing, giving pleasure

indicators.note: playing suggests the words are toyed with and their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A busking street band enjoys performing for the crowd's enjoyment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving' is a link word. BEER AND SKITTLES is a British idiom for easy enjoyment, usually in 'life isn't all beer and skittles'; skittles is a pub game like ninepins.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom denotes carefree fun and amusement, as in a life of ease.

clue.text: Withdraw religious education pamphlet

parts.note: RE is the school-subject abbreviation for religious education
a tract is a short pamphlet, often on a religious theme

explanation.surface: A church pamphlet is pulled from circulation.
explanation.definitionFit: To take back a statement is a synonym for withdrawing it.

clue.text: Suggest operation in writing

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language

explanation.surface: Someone recommends that a surgical procedure be put on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward an idea for consideration is to suggest it.

clue.text: Conservative with round middle is source of jokes

parts.note: O is round in shape
median means middle, as in the central value

explanation.surface: A Tory with a paunch provides all the laughs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round middle' reads as a pot belly, but 'round' gives O and 'middle' gives MEDIAN separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-up performer is the person who delivers the gags.

clue.text: A hotline out of order in comic opera

indicators.note: out of order suggests the letters are not in their proper sequence

explanation.surface: A broken telephone hotline features in a comic opera.
explanation.walkthrough: IOLANTHE is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's fairy work is a well-known example of comic opera.

clue.text: Business rated badly

indicators.note: badly suggests the word is put together wrongly, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A company has received a poor review score.
explanation.definitionFit: Commerce or a line of work is a synonym for business.

clue.text: Get to know when sure

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'
certain means sure

explanation.surface: You learn something once you are confident of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To find out for certain is to discover or learn a fact.

clue.text: Musical group that's needed for board meeting?

parts.note: Chess is a stage musical by Benny Andersson, Björn Ulvaeus and Tim Rice
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A band is required for a company directors' meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical group' looks like a band, but splits into the musical CHESS and the group. 'board meeting' is pieces meeting on a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The pieces and board are what two players require for a game on the chequered squares.

clue.text: Former monarch and husband rejected hair dye

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Queen Anne reigned in Britain from 1702 to 1714

explanation.surface: A past queen and her consort turned down a hair colouring product.
explanation.definitionFit: This reddish-brown plant extract is used to colour hair and skin.

clue.text: Stupid offence, one committed by an employee at the start

indicators.note: committed by means placed in the keeping of, so these go inside the other letters

parts.note: a sin is an offence
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: at the start says take the opening letter of employee

explanation.surface: A worker commits a foolish offence at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'committed by' puts SINI inside ANE (an plus the first letter of employee).
explanation.definitionFit: Foolish and silly behaviour is senseless, a synonym for stupid.

clue.text: Get beaten by mug, be humiliated

parts.note: to lose is to be beaten
mug is slang for the face

explanation.surface: Someone loses a fight to a thug and is shamed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to suffer a loss of dignity or reputation.

clue.text: Wild about editor's form of government?

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: feral means wild
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about an editor's style of governance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' reads as angry but gives FERAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A system in which states share power with a central authority is a type of government.

clue.text: Guide showing king round centre of Aden

indicators.note: round says the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king

indicators.note: centre of says take the middle letters of the word Aden

explanation.surface: A tour guide takes a king around the middle of Aden, the Yemeni port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' wraps Shakespeare's king around the two central letters of Aden.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who heads or directs others acts as a guide.

clue.text: Broadcasting organisation in King's Cross, say

definitions.meaning: a radio or TV channel or company
King's Cross is a major London railway terminus

explanation.surface: A broadcaster is based in a London district.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcaster is a radio or television outlet, and a railway terminus is a stop for trains.

clue.text: Main artery forming part of that road heading north

indicators.note: heading north says the hidden letters are read backwards
forming part of says the letters are a section inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A main road heading north is part of a trunk route network.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'forming part' in the definition; it signals the hidden word, so the definition is just 'Main artery'. In a down clue 'heading north' reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest artery carries blood from the heart, so it is the main one.

clue.text: Finish with awfully sore back

parts.note: an end is a finish

indicators.note: awfully suggests the word is badly mangled, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone ends up with a painful back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like part of the sore body part, but it is the definition, a verb meaning support. 'awfully' turns SORE into ORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To support a candidate or product publicly is a synonym for backing it.

clue.text: Petite female engulfed by rising river

indicators.note: engulfed by says the first letter sits inside the other piece
rising in a down clue means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the Nile is the great African river

explanation.surface: A small woman is swept up by a flooding river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns NILE into ELIN, and F goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin describes someone small and delicate, like a fairy.

clue.text: Even leading may be child's play

parts.note: straight means level or even
forward means at the front, leading

explanation.surface: Even a frontrunner's position may be a game for children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' is a link word. 'Even' reads as an adverb but is an adjective meaning level.
explanation.definitionFit: Something simple and uncomplicated is described as easy as a game for kids.

clue.text: Difficult question from guy by river

parts.note: to guy is to mock or make fun of, to tease

explanation.surface: A man by the riverside poses a tricky puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' looks like a noun meaning man, but it is the verb meaning ridicule.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain-teaser is a hard puzzle or tricky problem.

clue.text: Short joke about English ship

parts.note: on means about, concerning
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A quick gag about a British vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A quip delivered in a single sentence is a brief witticism.
